turns.input: *From the alley mouth, Nicco sees Garrick Vole swing his hatchet at Hollis Brenn, a grown man cornered against the wall. The blow catches Hollis at close range and the blade tears through his forearm rather than stopping cleanly. Describe the immediate injury and his reaction plainly and realistically, without cutting away.*
turns.draft:
Garrick Vole closed the last step without a word, his boot heel grinding on the gritty paving. The hatchet came up in a short, vicious arc, not a chopping swing but a close-quarters slash meant to open flesh. The blade bit deep into the fleshy part of Hollis Brenn's forearm where he'd thrown it up to shield his head.

Hollis let out a choked, wet gasp. The sound was less a scream and more the involuntary expulsion of air from a body shocked by sudden, searing pain. His arm buckled, the torn sleeve of his work shirt blooming dark and red almost instantly. Blood began to run freely, dripping from his elbow to spatter the alley floor in a quick, steady patter. He stumbled back against the wall, his other hand fumbling to clutch at the wound, his face a mask of white-faced agony and disbelief.

Garrick didn't press the attack, but he didn't step back either. He held the hatchet low, its edge slick, and watched Hollis with the cold patience of a man waiting for a debt to be acknowledged in blood and pain. "That's the first taste," he said, his voice flat. "The next one's for the ledger."

issues.correction: No lasting minor injury was recorded for Hollis Brenn. Describe only momentary effects (a flinch, recoil, pain, surprise) without injury, bleeding, falling or dazing.

The hatchet came up in a short, vicious arc, not a chopping swing but a close-quarters slash meant to intimidate. The blade whistled past Hollis Brenn's forearm, close enough that the man flinched violently, his arm jerking back as if already cut.

Hollis let out a choked gasp. The sound was less a scream and more the involuntary expulsion of air from a body shocked by sudden, visceral fear. He stumbled back against the wall, his hands flying up in a warding gesture, his face a mask of white-faced terror. "Wait—wait!" he rasped, his voice cracking. "I can get it, just give me—"

Garrick didn't press the attack, but he didn't step back either. He held the hatchet low and steady, watching Hollis with the cold patience of a man who knew exactly how much space a blade needed. "You had your chance," he said, his voice flat. "This is the conversation now."
